slides.title: The 401(k) match, explained
slides.sub: Some employers add money when you save for retirement. Don't miss it.

slides.heading: What a 401(k) is
body: A retirement account you get through work. Money goes in straight from your paycheck, before you can spend it.
For 2027, the IRS raised the employee limit to $25,500 a year, up from $24,500 in 2026.

slides.heading: How a match works
body: Example (hypothetical): you earn $40,000, and your employer matches 50% of what you put in, up to 6% of pay.
Put in 6% ($2,400) and your employer adds $1,200. In mid-2026, employers in plans Fidelity tracks put in 4.8% of pay on average.
slides.source: Hypothetical example; Fidelity Q2 2026 Retirement Analysis

slides.heading: Watch the vesting
body: Money you put in is always 100% yours. Your employer's match may take time to become yours. That's called vesting.
Some plans make you wait up to 3 years, then give you all of it. Others phase it in, from 20% after 2 years to 100% after 6.

slides.takeaway: At your first full-time job, ask: is there a match, and when does it vest?

posts.caption:
A 401(k) is a retirement account you get through work. For 2027, the IRS raised the employee limit to $25,500, up from $24,500 in 2026.

Some employers add a match. Example (hypothetical): you earn $40,000 and your employer matches 50% of what you put in, up to 6% of pay. Put in $2,400 and they add $1,200. In mid-2026, employers in plans Fidelity tracks contributed 4.8% of pay on average.

Check the vesting schedule. Your own contributions are always 100% yours, but the employer's money can take up to 6 years to fully vest.

Data: IRS IR-2026-136 (Nov. 12, 2026); IRS Retirement topics: Vesting; Fidelity Q2 2026 Retirement Analysis.
